title: Vexa — end-to-end workflow
subtitle: How an owner sets Vexa up, how every call is answered, understood and acted on, and what happens after it ends. Each box names the exact code path, model, API or data store involved; numbered badges match the step-by-step walkthrough below.

meta.v: UC1 Set up the assistant · UC2 Answer a call (live phone calls and in-app test calls) · UC3 After the call. Personal and Business modes share the same pipeline.

github.com/Phani3108/Vexa · branch `launch-l0` · commit `10c45ad` · 29 Oct 2026 · backend/src, web/src, backend/.env.example, Dockerfile, docker-compose.yml, .github/workflows, backend/test, backend/eval
From ROADMAP.md (India-first plan): Indian speech engines and voices, Indian phone number, WhatsApp, UPI, calendar and CRM. Drawn as Not integrated.

Text understanding, flows, analysis, translation and the app run end to end today. The live phone path (Twilio + OpenAI Realtime) is complete in code but has not been run on a real call: no Twilio or OpenAI keys are configured.
Phani Marupaka with Claude Code · 29 Oct 2026

phases.text: Outside the system: the owner forwards calls from their carrier to the Vexa Twilio number

lanes.title: People and UI
lanes.subtitle: what owners and callers see and do

boxes.title: Sign in with a phone number
boxes.body: Enters a number, receives a 6-digit code. `POST /api/auth/otp/request` → `POST /api/auth/otp/verify`.

boxes.title: Verify code, issue tokens
boxes.body: Code stored as SHA-256 hash, 10-minute expiry, 5 attempts. Issues JWT access (7 days) and refresh (30 days). First login creates the account (id = phone number).

boxes.title: Send the code
boxes.body: `verify.v2.services(…).verifications` when `TWILIO_VERIFY_SERVICE_SID` is set, else `messages.create`. In development the code is returned on screen instead (`devCode`).

boxes.title: Codes and accounts
boxes.body: TTL index deletes expired codes. Embedded MongoDB in development (`backend/.data/mongo`); `MONGODB_URI` required in production.

boxes.title: Rate limits and secret checks
boxes.body: Code requests 5 per 15 min per IP and phone; checks 20 per 15 min. Production refuses to start with a missing or default `JWT_SECRET`.

boxes.title: Choose mode and teach Vexa the business
boxes.body: Personal or Business, industry template, hours, catalog (stock, price), FAQs, VIPs, greeting language, recording. `POST /api/users/onboarding`, `PUT /api/users/config`, `PUT /api/workflows/:id`.

boxes.title: 17 built-in call flows
boxes.body: 10 business (booking, quote, stock & price, directions, emergency…) and 7 personal (delivery, bank & loan, family, spam…). Edited flows are validated: known step types, valid targets, at least one end step, `maxTurns` 2–20.

boxes.title: Ask Vexa commands
boxes.body: `assistantService.runCommand` → `structuredJson(COMMAND_SCHEMA)`: "Focus until 7 pm", "block that number", "tell Dana her parts arrived". Offline grammar if the model is unavailable. `POST /api/assistant/command`.

boxes.title: Owner settings and caller notes
boxes.body: Business profile and catalog, VIP and blocked numbers, shield (standard, focus, aggressive, silent), recording {on, announce, keep 90 days}, notes to pass on next call.

boxes.title: Whitelisted edits and caps
boxes.body: Only `EDITABLE_FIELDS` can change. Ask Vexa 30/min, at most 5 actions, Focus capped at 7 days. Built-in flows can't be deleted; the fallback flow can't be turned off.

boxes.tag: Caller · any phone · or owner test call
boxes.title: Someone calls the owner
boxes.body: The carrier forwards the call to the Vexa Twilio number. Owners can also run a test call in the app (`POST /api/simulator/start`), typed or by browser mic.

boxes.title: Screen before answering
boxes.body: `POST /voice/incoming-call`: finds the owner, reads caller memory, VIP, Focus and hours, scores spam risk. Blocked numbers, and risk ≥ 80 on the aggressive shield, are rejected before any AI cost. Returns TwiML `<Connect><Stream>`.

boxes.title: Speak the greeting
boxes.body: Says the engine's greeting exactly (VIPs by name), plus "This call may be recorded." unless the owner turned the notice off. Translated to the owner's greeting language.

boxes.title: Webhooks and media stream
boxes.body: `POST /voice/incoming-call`, `POST /voice/call-status`; WebSocket `/voice/media-stream` carries 8 kHz μ-law audio both ways.

boxes.title: Who is this caller?
boxes.body: Caller record, last 5 calls from the number, last 5 in the same category: name, summary so far, notes to deliver, always-transfer, spam count. Test calls never read or write memory.

boxes.title: Signature, risk score, shields
boxes.body: Twilio signature checked in production (`TWILIO_VALIDATE_SIGNATURE`). Call audio stream accepted only with a single-use token signed for that call (`lib/streamToken.js`), else closed. Risk score 0–100 (no caller ID, past spam, call bursts, spoofing).

boxes.title: Watch the call live
boxes.body: Transcript, facts filling in, caller's language, all over Socket.io (`call:transcript`, `call:language`).

boxes.title: Clean the transcript, one turn at a time
boxes.body: Drops noise, greeting echo, URLs, gibberish and the fragment after an interruption; ignores "haan"/"hmm" said over Vexa. Test calls enter at `POST /api/simulator/:id/message`.

boxes.title: Speech to text
boxes.body: Transcribes the caller inside the Realtime session. Server VAD 0.6, 700 ms silence. On flow calls the model never replies on its own (`create_response:false`).

boxes.title: Per-turn understanding
boxes.body: `nlu.understand()`: flow, facts in English, answer from business info, emergency, wants a person, language, mixed with English, English translation, yes/no. Hard timeout `NLU_TIMEOUT_MS` (5 s).

boxes.title: Active call state
boxes.body: `VoiceAgent.activeCalls`: context, flow session, transcript, recording buffer. Lost on restart; test sessions expire after 30 min.

boxes.title: Offline understanding fallback
boxes.body: On timeout or error the rules in `extractors.js` + `indic.js` answer: lakh/dedh, kal/parso, "5 baje", haan/avunu/illa, +91 numbers, Hinglish in English letters.

boxes.title: Indian-language test set
boxes.body: 161 cases + 50 held-out, 8 languages. Without the model 99% / 98%; with Claude 100% / 100%. `npm run eval:nlu`.

boxes.title: Hears the answer in their language
boxes.body: Telugu → Hindi → English mid-call is followed; Hinglish is answered in Hinglish; prices and totals come from the catalog.

boxes.title: Decide the next step
boxes.body: Emergency switch → pick the flow → confirm or correct → answer side questions → fill several facts at once → next step: ask, confirm, catalog lookup, branch, act, transfer, end.

boxes.title: Grounded directions
boxes.body: Delivery flow only: `groundedDirections()` turns the saved address and gate notes into directions from where the courier is. "Use ONLY the facts provided"; 6 s; template if it fails.

boxes.title: Speak the reply
boxes.body: `speakInstruction`: the engine's English line spoken in the caller's language, mixed with English if they mix. Voice from owner settings.

boxes.title: Reply translation (test calls)
boxes.body: `translateText` writes the reply in the caller's language and script. Skipped on live calls (the voice translates). Falls back to English.

boxes.title: Catalog and business facts
boxes.body: Stock, unit price, aliases; address, directions, hours, FAQs. The only facts Vexa may state.

boxes.title: Engine limits and answer rules
boxes.body: 10 turns max, 2 re-asks then a partial message; answers only from business info; owner text sanitized against prompt injection; caller cuts in only after 600 ms (`BARGE_IN_MS`).

boxes.title: Pick up, or steer the call
boxes.body: "Pick up or let Vexa handle it" (`call:handoff`). Send a note, ask for email, transfer, end: `POST /voice/whisper`, `/voice/takeover`, `/voice/end-call`.

boxes.title: Decide who gets through
boxes.body: VIPs and always-transfer callers; emergencies (unless after-hours transfer is off); never during Focus; business numbers only when open. Owner-only (`ownedCall`).

boxes.title: Bridge the owner in
boxes.body: Caller moved into `<Dial><Conference>`; owner dialed with a spoken summary; hang up with `calls(sid).update`.

boxes.title: Push to the owner's phone
boxes.body: `admin.messaging().send`: live call, urgent, summary. Needs `FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT`; off otherwise.

boxes.title: Live events to the app
boxes.body: Room `user:<id>`: transcript, language, handoff, urgent, booking requested, analyzed.

boxes.title: Emergencies always win
boxes.body: Escalation words or the model's emergency flag switch to the Emergency flow and alert the owner during the call. Silent shield stops pushes.

boxes.title: Close the record
boxes.body: Builds the bilingual transcript, runs analysis, lets the flow's facts win for lead, name and spam, updates caller memory (real calls only), saves the cost ledger as `aiUsage`.

boxes.title: Post-call analysis
boxes.body: `ConversationAnalyzer`: category, summary, sentiment, urgency, lead, spam. 30 s; keyword fallback if it fails.

boxes.title: Transcript and summary translation
boxes.body: `translateLines`: every line to English in one request. `translateText`: summary in the caller's language and script (`summaryLocal`).

boxes.title: Call history written
boxes.body: Transcript (as spoken + English), analysis, flow run, languages, AI usage, recording metadata; caller summary and spam counts.

boxes.title: Call recording
boxes.body: Stereo WAV, caller left and Vexa right, from the media stream; 2-hour cap. Deleted after `retentionDays` (default 90). Docker keeps them on a `recordings` volume.

boxes.title: Quality signals on every call
boxes.body: Model used or not per turn (`aiAssisted`), latency, tokens and cost by purpose, questions asked and skipped, risk score, status of every action.

boxes.title: Read, listen, act
boxes.body: Summary in English + caller's language, bilingual transcript, "Read in…" 8 languages, recording player (tap a line to jump), approve bookings, send the reply.

boxes.title: Outcomes
boxes.body: Add to inbox, booking request, text the caller, notify the owner, mark spam. Each records done, sent, simulated, skipped or failed.

boxes.title: Read the call in any language
boxes.body: `POST /api/calls/:id/translate`: whole call and summary in any of 8 languages; saved in `Call.translations`, so it's paid once.

boxes.title: Texts to the caller
boxes.body: `messages.create` (≤ 640 chars): booking confirmed or declined, reply drafts. Simulated for test calls; skipped if Twilio isn't configured.

boxes.title: Calendar, CRM, WhatsApp, UPI
boxes.body: Bookings are requests, not calendar slots; no CRM sync, WhatsApp messages or payment links yet.

boxes.title: Owner approves; links expire
boxes.body: AI only requests bookings; the owner confirms (`PATCH /api/bookings/:id`). Recordings play through 15-minute signed links; audio can be deleted per call.

boxes.title: Test suites
boxes.body: 47 backend tests and the offline understanding gate (≥ 97%, held-out ≥ 95%) run in GitHub Actions with the web build and Docker image. 9 mobile tests. **Partial:** no web unit tests yet.

footnote: Flows decide; models only read and speak. Optional = needs a credential to switch on. In memory = lost on restart. Not integrated = planned, not in code.

items.text: The owner opens the Vexa app (installable web app, or the mobile app) and enters a phone number. The app calls `POST /api/auth/otp/request`, then `POST /api/auth/otp/verify` with the 6-digit code.
The server stores only a hash of the code, accepts it for 10 minutes and allows 5 tries. A correct code returns a 7-day access token and a 30-day refresh token. The first login creates the account.
The code is sent by Twilio Verify, or as a plain Twilio SMS. In development no SMS is sent and the code is shown on screen.
Codes and accounts live in MongoDB. Expired codes delete themselves.
Rate limits stop code guessing and SMS abuse, and production will not start with a weak signing secret.

steps.group: UC1 · Configure flows, business and languages

items.text: The owner picks Personal or Business, an industry template, opening hours, a product catalog with stock and prices, FAQs, VIP contacts, the greeting language and recording settings.
Vexa ships 17 ready-made call flows. Owners can edit them step by step; every edit is checked before it is saved, so a flow can't loop or dead-end.
Owners can also just say what they want ("I'm busy until 7 pm", "block that number"). Claude turns that into actions; a rule-based parser takes over if Claude is unavailable.
Settings, the catalog, shields and notes for specific callers are stored in MongoDB.
Only approved fields can be edited, commands are rate-limited and capped, and the built-in safety flows can't be removed.
A caller dials the owner. The owner's carrier forwards the call to the Vexa Twilio number. Owners can rehearse the same pipeline with an in-app test call.

Before answering, Vexa finds the owner, recalls the caller, checks VIPs, Focus and business hours, and scores spam risk. Blocked or very risky callers are rejected before any AI cost. Twilio is told to stream the audio to Vexa.
The OpenAI Realtime voice speaks the greeting written by the flow engine, including the recording notice.
Twilio sends call events to Vexa's webhooks and streams the audio in both directions over a WebSocket.
Caller history is read: their name, what past calls were about, any note the owner left for them, and whether they are usually spam.

Twilio signatures are verified in production, and the call's audio stream is only accepted with a single-use token signed for that exact call. The risk score and the owner's shield decide how strict to be.
The owner can watch the call live: the transcript, the facts Vexa has captured and the caller's language.
Each caller sentence is cleaned (noise, echoes and false starts are dropped) and processed in order, one turn at a time.
OpenAI turns the caller's speech into text. On flow calls the voice model never answers on its own; the flow engine decides every reply.
Claude reads each sentence and returns structured facts in English: which flow, names, dates, quantities, any question, an emergency, the language and an English translation. It has 5 seconds.
The live call's state is kept in server memory and is lost if the server restarts.
If Claude is slow or down, built-in rules understand Indian numbers, dates, yes/no and phone numbers in eight languages, so the call keeps going.
This understanding is measured on 211 test sentences in eight languages, including 50 held back from tuning.
The caller hears the answer in the language they are using right now, even when they switch mid-call.

The flow engine, not the model, decides what happens next: switch to emergency, confirm, answer a side question, look up stock and price, transfer or end. Several facts can be captured from one sentence.
For deliveries, Claude writes directions to the owner's home from the courier's location, using only the saved address and gate notes.
The voice speaks the engine's line in the caller's language, mixing in English the way the caller does.
On test calls, Claude translates the reply in text; on live calls the voice does it, which saves a request.
Prices, stock, hours, address and FAQs come from the owner's profile, so Vexa never guesses a number.
Calls are capped at 10 turns, unanswered questions end in a message for the owner, and answers are limited to the owner's own business information.
When a call needs the owner, their app asks "pick up, or let Vexa handle it?". During any call the owner can send Vexa a note, ask it to collect an email, transfer or end the call.
Clear rules decide who gets through: VIPs and chosen callers, emergencies, nobody during Focus, and business calls only during opening hours.
To transfer, Twilio moves the caller into a conference and calls the owner with a short spoken summary first.
Push notifications go to the owner's phone through Firebase, when it is configured.
All live updates reach the owner's app over an authenticated Socket.io connection.
Emergencies always override other settings and alert the owner while the call is still going.
When the call ends, Vexa builds a transcript with every line as spoken plus English, saves the outcome, updates what it knows about the caller and records the exact AI cost.
Claude summarises the call: category, summary, urgency, whether it is a lead or spam.
Claude translates the transcript into English and writes the summary in the caller's language too.
Everything is saved in MongoDB as the call history that future calls draw on.
The recording is saved as a stereo audio file (on a persistent volume in Docker) and deleted automatically after the owner's retention period.
Every call carries quality signals: whether the model was used each turn, latency, tokens and cost by purpose, and how many questions were skipped.
The owner reads the call in English and the caller's language, listens to the recording, approves bookings and sends a reply.
Each outcome (inbox, booking request, text, alert, spam tag) is recorded with whether it was done, simulated or skipped.
The owner can read any call in any of the eight languages; the translation is saved, so it is paid for once.
Confirmation texts and replies go out by Twilio SMS. Test calls only simulate them.
Calendar booking, CRM sync, WhatsApp and UPI payment links are planned, not built.
A person approves every booking, and recordings can only be played through short-lived links.
Every change runs 47 backend tests, the understanding test gate, the web build and the Docker build in CI; 9 mobile tests also exist.

sections.title: Known gaps (from the code)
bullets: The live phone path (Twilio + OpenAI Realtime) is complete in code but has not run on a real call; no keys are configured.
Active calls, test sessions and rate-limit counters live in memory: one server instance only, and a restart drops live calls.
Per-turn replies take 2–9 s on Opus; a fast model (e.g. Haiku) is recommended for live calls.
